details: CONFIRMED by running it. The brief gave this line as an example ("e.g."), so the fixer may change it. relay requires python3 3.11+ (README, deps.toml) and every entry point uses #!/usr/bin/env python3 or calls python3 by name, so the first python3 on PATH decides. Prepending the developer-tools bin folder makes that Apple's 3.9.6.
A git-only folder works: a directory with one symlink, git -> $(xcrun --find git), first on PATH. The symlink also avoids the first-run scan cost of section 2 (no new executable is written).
Severity HIGH: the doc's one recommended action breaks relay on ordinary use for any Mac reader who follows it.
evidence: $ ln -sf /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/git <scratch>/gitbin/git; PATH="<scratch>/gitbin:$PATH" sh -c 'command -v git; git --version; git --exec-path; command -v python3'
failing_case: On this Mac, a reader follows the doc and adds export PATH="$(dirname "$(xcrun --find git)"):$PATH" to the shell profile.
The prepended folder /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin (and /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin with only the CLT) also holds python3, pip3, make, ld.

Now: command -v python3 -> /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/python3 (Python 3.9.6); ./bin/relay help -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib'. Every relay command, every python3 hook (merge.py, check-mark.py, turn-limit.py ...) and bin/ci (calls python3) break.
Should: the fix speeds up git only and leaves python3 (and the other tools) resolving as before: /opt/homebrew/bin/python3, 3.11+.
fix_hint: Replace the line with a folder that holds only git, e.g.
and one sentence on why not the whole folder (it carries Apple's python3 3.9, older than relay needs).
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the fix shown in docs/macos.md section 1, applied in a shell where command -v python3 was /opt/homebrew/bin/python3, leaves command -v python3 unchanged and ./bin/relay help runs.

2. Artifact: the same fix makes command -v git print a path that is not /usr/bin/git and git --version reports the developer tools' git (checked: a folder holding only a symlink to $(xcrun --find git) gives git version 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), exec-path /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/libexec/git-core, git log works).
3. Artifact: the doc says why the whole developer-tools folder must not go first on PATH (it carries python3 3.9).
4. Artifact: the Homebrew alternative and the owner decision line (relay does not change PATH) stay.
reason: docs/macos.md:16-26 git-only symlink folder and the python3 3.9 warning; tests/test_macos_doc.py:11,15,20 pass; first two fail on the old doc.
findings.summary: the recommended PATH line puts Apple's python3 3.9.6 ahead of every other python3, and relay then fails to start (needs 3.11+)

details: CONFIRMED by arithmetic. Copied from the brief's wording; the doc is the place readers take numbers from. Size: 5 agent minutes.
failing_case: A reader of section 1 reads "Each start through the launcher costs 8-12 ms more: 11.8 ms against 4.1 ms". 11.8 - 4.1 = 7.7 ms, outside the stated 8-12 range; the sentence reads as if 8-12 were the difference.
Should: the range and the worked numbers agree (e.g. "about 8 ms more: 11.8 ms against 4.1 ms", or say what 8-12 is the range of).
fix_hint: "about 8 ms more per start: 11.8 ms against 4.1 ms ..."
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the stated extra cost and the two measured means in the same sentence agree (difference 7.7 ms, or a range that contains it).
2. Artifact: the 30 interleaved rounds and the 29,000 starts / 81% figures stay.
reason: docs/macos.md:9 "about 8 ms more: 11.8 ms against 4.1 ms"; tests/test_macos_doc.py:24 passes, fails on the old doc.
findings.summary: "8-12 ms more" is followed by its own example, 11.8 against 4.1 ms, which is 7.7 ms more

details: PLAUSIBLE that the intended meaning is interpreter start-up per spawned python process; not measured here. Size: 5 agent minutes (ask the front for the measurement's split if unknown).
failing_case: Section 3 says Python's own work is about 1.5% of the suite's time, then that a faster language would save at most 5-10%. A reader cannot see where the other 3.5-8.5% comes from (interpreter start-up per process? imports?), so the two numbers look contradictory.
Should: one clause says what the 5-10% counts beyond the 1.5% (or the bound is stated as what was measured).
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: section 3 names what the 5-10% upper bound includes beyond Python's own 1.5% (e.g. interpreter start-up and imports for each process).
2. Artifact: the conclusion (time goes to starting processes, git above all, the disk and the two macOS costs) stays.
reason: docs/macos.md:42 splits 1-1.5% own logic from 4-7% child interpreter starts = at most 5-10%; tests/test_macos_doc.py:31 passes, fails on the old doc.
findings.summary: Python is 1.5% of the time, yet a faster language would save "at most 5-10%": the gap is not explained
